metrics.label: Brent crude

metrics.label: WTI crude
metrics.blurb: The US crude benchmark. Its gap to Brent drives US export volumes.
metrics.fallback: CNBC live quote, then the daily oil report, then EIA/FRED

metrics.label: Henry Hub gas

metrics.label: Coal API2 (ARA)

metrics.label: Heating oil / gasoil

metrics.label: RBOB gasoline

metrics.label: Dry bulk ETF (BDRY)

metrics.label: Tanker ETF (BWET)
metrics.blurb: An ETF holding tanker freight futures. A rough daily read on tanker sentiment.

metrics.label: Baltic Capesize Index
metrics.blurb: The Capesize component of the Baltic Dry Index. The most volatile part, and effectively a bet on Chinese steel production.

metrics.label: Baltic Panamax Index
metrics.blurb: The Panamax component. Coal and grain rather than iron ore, so it follows harvests and power demand more than steel.

metrics.label: Baltic Supramax Index
metrics.blurb: The Supramax component. These ships have their own cranes and serve smaller ports, so it reflects broad trade rather than one commodity.

metrics.label: Baltic Dry Index
metrics.blurb: The Baltic Exchange's headline dry bulk freight index. Published late afternoon London time, so a morning brief shows the previous session.
metrics.source: Baltic Exchange via Hellenic Shipping News

metrics.label: VLSFO Singapore
metrics.blurb: Price of the main low-sulphur marine fuel at the world's biggest bunker port.

metrics.label: VLSFO Rotterdam
metrics.blurb: The same fuel in Europe's biggest bunker port.

metrics.label: VLSFO Fujairah
metrics.blurb: The Middle East bunker hub, where most VLCC voyages refuel.

metrics.label: Diesel crack vs Brent
metrics.blurb: Roughly what a refinery makes turning a barrel of crude into diesel. Computed as the gasoil price converted to barrels minus Brent. Fat margins make refineries run hard, which creates product tanker cargo.

metrics.label: Brent–WTI spread
metrics.blurb: How much more Brent costs than WTI. A wide gap makes exporting US crude profitable, which means more long-haul cargoes and stronger tanker demand.

rates.label: VLCC (TD3C, AG→China)

rates.label: Suezmax (TD20, W.Africa→UKC)

brief.text:
The weekend brought a fresh round of violence around the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway at the mouth of the Arabian Gulf through which much of the world's crude moves. Seatrade reports crew abandoned a tanker in Hormuz and US forces struck a bulker in the Gulf of Oman, Iranian media suggested blasts in southern Iran were Iranian military activity rather than US strikes, and Houthi forces hit Saudi Aramco's headquarters building. For anyone fixing tankers out of the Gulf today, that means war-risk and crew-safety questions on every Arabian Gulf voyage before you talk rate. Separately, Iraq's foreign minister said Baghdad has reached understandings with Washington to allow Iraqi oil exports through Hormuz via a shipping lane near Oman.

On prices, Brent crude is 96.68 USD/bbl today, down 1.64 (-1.7%), and WTI is 89.79, down 1.04 (-1.1%), with the Brent-WTI spread at 6.89. Notably, crude fell while bunkers — the fuel ships burn — rose at all four hubs: Houston VLSFO 770.50 USD/t (+16.50, +2.2%), Fujairah 865.00 (+13.50, +1.6%), Rotterdam 739.50 (+7.50, +1.0%), Singapore 854.00 (+4.50, +0.5%). The data here does not show why crude softened against a weekend of Gulf attacks, nor why bunkers diverged; do not assume a link. Higher bunker prices raise voyage costs and cut TCE, the time-charter-equivalent daily earnings an owner nets after bunkers and port costs. No freight index refreshed today: the Baltic Dry Index stood at 2,805 points on Friday 6 November (+65, +2.4%), the Capesize index — Capesizes being the largest dry bulk ships, typically iron ore and coal — at 4,097 on Wednesday 4 November, and VLCC TD3C earnings at 1,303,616 USD/day on Sunday 8 November.

Running stories: the Hormuz attack story developed today with the abandoned tanker, the Gulf of Oman strike and the Aramco headquarters hit. The Black Sea story also developed — Russia said its forces hit three cargo vessels carrying military goods for Ukraine. The shadow-fleet story advanced, with ARACON hearing that 25% of the internationally trading crude fleet now sits on the dark list. US and European port labour disruption had no news today and is unchanged, as is the Russian diesel export story.

Watch whether Iraqi exports actually move through the Oman-side lane, since that changes Gulf loading patterns, and watch whether bunker premiums at Fujairah and Houston hold.

storylines.title: Attacks and blockade enforcement around Hormuz
storylines.what: Attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz have continued into November. Over the weekend crew abandoned a tanker in Hormuz, US forces struck a bulker in the Gulf of Oman, Iranian media attributed blasts in southern Iran to Iranian military activity, and Houthi forces hit Saudi Aramco's headquarters building.
storylines.why_it_matters: Hull strikes, crew abandonment and armed enforcement raise war-risk premiums and crew-safety objections for Arabian Gulf liftings, shrinking the pool of willing owners and supporting tanker earnings.

storylines.title: Sanctions and evasion in the shadow fleet
storylines.what: US sanctions have expanded across Cuban maritime and energy entities and Iranian false-flag registry networks, while analysts describe the dark fleet as a parallel fleet that has tripled in size since 2022.
storylines.why_it_matters: Registry fraud, AIS spoofing and blocked-property designations force charterers, insurers and class societies to re-verify documentation and positions, pushing tonnage out of mainstream trades and tightening compliant tanker supply.
storylines.latest: ARACON heard that 25% of the internationally trading crude oil fleet now sits on the dark list.
sources: ARACON: 25% of the internationally-trading crude oil fleet now sits on the dark list

storylines.title: Attacks on shipping in the Black Sea
storylines.what: A Greek container ship sank after being hit by naval drones off Bulgaria, and Russia says its forces hit three cargo vessels it claims were carrying military goods for Ukraine, along with two electricity substations.
storylines.why_it_matters: Strikes on ships and port infrastructure threaten grain and dry bulk loadings from the region and add insurance and routing costs for any vessel calling there.
storylines.latest: Russia said overnight strikes hit three cargo vessels and two electricity substations.
sources: Russia Says It Hit Three Cargo Ships In Black Sea

storylines.title: Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab transits and Gulf congestion
storylines.what: Hormuz traffic rose in October to its highest monthly level since July, supported by dry bulk and LNG even as VLCC traffic declined, with Red Sea traffic up and Arabian Gulf waiting elevated. Iraq now says it has reached understandings with the US to export oil through Hormuz via a lane near Oman.
storylines.why_it_matters: Transit counts, routing lanes and waiting times determine voyage lengths, tonne-mile demand and effective fleet supply.
storylines.latest: Iraq's foreign minister said Baghdad has understandings with Washington allowing Iraqi oil exports through Hormuz via a shipping lane near Oman.
sources: Iraq Has Reached Understandings With US To Allow Oil Exports Through Hormuz

storylines.title: Port labour disruption in the US and Europe
storylines.what: A contract standoff involving about 250 security workers threatens operations across Los Angeles and Long Beach terminals, while dockworkers have struck across Europe and beyond over arms shipments.
storylines.why_it_matters: Labour action at container and ferry berths disrupts berthing schedules and cargo flows, and the unresolved US West Coast dispute leaves a large share of US import capacity exposed to stoppage.

storylines.title: Russian diesel flows and export restrictions
storylines.what: A reported US-Russia agreement on supplying extra diesel to the US market has met political opposition, while Russia has extended a general ban on most diesel exports until the end of January, with some volumes still allowed to flow.
storylines.why_it_matters: Diesel export restrictions and any reopened Atlantic route reshape clean product tanker ton-miles and MR and LR employment patterns.

storylines.title: Sanctions and evasion in the shadow fleet
storylines.what: US sanctions have expanded across Cuban maritime and energy entities and Iranian false-flag registry networks, while analysts describe the dark fleet as a parallel fleet that has tripled in size since 2022.
storylines.why_it_matters: Registry fraud, AIS spoofing and blocked-property designations force charterers, insurers and class societies to re-verify documentation and positions, pushing tonnage out of mainstream trades and tightening compliant tanker supply.
storylines.latest: ARACON heard that 25% of the internationally trading crude oil fleet now sits on the dark list.
sources: ARACON: 25% of the internationally-trading crude oil fleet now sits on the dark list

storylines.title: Attacks on shipping in the Black Sea
storylines.what: A Greek container ship sank after being hit by naval drones off Bulgaria, and Russia says its forces hit three cargo vessels it claims were carrying military goods for Ukraine, along with two electricity substations.
storylines.why_it_matters: Strikes on ships and port infrastructure threaten grain and dry bulk loadings from the region and add insurance and routing costs for any vessel calling there.
storylines.latest: Russia said overnight strikes hit three cargo vessels and two electricity substations.
sources: Russia Says It Hit Three Cargo Ships In Black Sea

storylines.title: Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab transits and Gulf congestion
storylines.what: Hormuz traffic rose in October to its highest monthly level since July, supported by dry bulk and LNG even as VLCC traffic declined, with Red Sea traffic up and Arabian Gulf waiting elevated. Iraq now says it has reached understandings with the US to export oil through Hormuz via a lane near Oman.
storylines.why_it_matters: Transit counts, routing lanes and waiting times determine voyage lengths, tonne-mile demand and effective fleet supply.
storylines.latest: Iraq's foreign minister said Baghdad has understandings with Washington allowing Iraqi oil exports through Hormuz via a shipping lane near Oman.
sources: Iraq Has Reached Understandings With US To Allow Oil Exports Through Hormuz

storylines.title: Port labour disruption in the US and Europe
storylines.what: A contract standoff involving about 250 security workers threatens operations across Los Angeles and Long Beach terminals, while dockworkers have struck across Europe and beyond over arms shipments.
storylines.why_it_matters: Labour action at container and ferry berths disrupts berthing schedules and cargo flows, and the unresolved US West Coast dispute leaves a large share of US import capacity exposed to stoppage.

storylines.title: Russian diesel flows and export restrictions
storylines.what: A reported US-Russia agreement on supplying extra diesel to the US market has met political opposition, while Russia has extended a general ban on most diesel exports until the end of January, with some volumes still allowed to flow.
storylines.why_it_matters: Diesel export restrictions and any reopened Atlantic route reshape clean product tanker ton-miles and MR and LR employment patterns.
